title: Nazariya
body: NGO Tammana, a leading non-profit organization dedicated to improving lives, visited the Institute for Blind, Sector 26, Chandigarh on 3rd August as part of their Event # 157, ‘Nazariya’, to engage with & motivate the visually impaired individuals and raise awareness about eye donation amongst the volunteers and the public.
Event SPOC Simran Bhatia ,shared that the team gained insights into the challenges faced by the visually impaired community but more of they celebrated their unique strengths and abilities.’
NGO’s founder Isha Kakaria also gave first hand valuable insights to the team members on the importance of eye donation and its potential to transform lives.

The strength of 170 students present astonished everyone during the interaction where they shared their goals. The team was sensitive on sharing empathy but not pitty and the students deserve as much equal respect and dignity.

She further remarked, “We often focus on what visually impaired individuals can’t do, but the event allowed us to see firsthand what they can do. Our goal is to ensure they have every opportunity to thrive.”

The visit highlighted several areas where visually impaired individuals often excel in terms of enhanced memory, improved tactile sensitivity, exceptional musical abilities with added resilience and adaptability.
The engagement was complemented by handy refreshments brought in by the NGO members to the event.

Member Manoj Dhania, expressed that ‘What struck me most was the incredible resilience and talent displayed by the students here. It’s crucial that we as a society recognize and nurture their strengths.”

It was emphasized that while 80% of visual impairment is preventable or treatable, there remains a significant need for corneal transplants. Eye donation can help address this gap and provide a second chance at sight for many.
Meenakshi Mahajan, Office Coordinator of the NGO,

“Team’s visit to the Institute for Blind has been truly inspiring. We’re committed to supporting the visually impaired community and spreading awareness about the critical need for eye donation. Just one person’s decision to donate their eyes can give the gift of sight to two individuals.”
Additionally, she stated, the event also gave an opportunity for team members to present a session on “Beti padhao, beti bachao” initiative.

Through this event, Tammana took a small but meaningful step towards creating a more inclusive society where visual impairment is not a limitation, but merely a different way of experiencing and contributing to the world. Every act of support, no matter how small, has the power to transform lives and brighten futures.

title: Open Air Yoga & Meditation
body: In a moment that transcended weather and time, Tammana NGO organized an open yoga event on 11th August 2024 at Fragrance Garden, Sector 36 Chandigarh that will be remembered for its beauty and serenity. As participants left their homes, undeterred by the possibility of rain, they felt a special calling—a pull that led them to something extraordinary.

As the soft breeze welcomed everyone with open arms, the connection with nature deepened, and it felt like a warm embrace. The gentle raindrops that kissed the faces and bodies of the participants during Shavasana brought a sense of inner peace, manifesting in smiles that spoke of pure contentment.

Inspiration was everywhere, with a shared determination that knew no bounds—regardless of age or gender. When the drizzle intensified, no one budged; the yoga instructor continued with unwavering focus, and it felt meant to be. It was a divine experience, where every soul present felt the unity and sanctity of the moment.

The event stretched over two hours, yet no one wished to leave. The participants relived the joy of childhood, running and playing on the wet grass with bare feet, their spirits rejuvenated. It was as if their inner child had come alive once more.

The instructor’s parting words resonated deeply: “लोग तो तरस जाते हैं, rain योग के लिए, you got it luckily.” It was a gift, a rare blessing to practice yoga under such conditions. The age-old saying, “जो जागत है सो पावत है,” came true for everyone present.

body: NGO Tammana Brings Christmas Cheer and Essential Support to children fighting Cancer.
In the spirit of spreading joy this holiday season, NGO Tammana organized a heartwarming Christmas celebration for the residents of Hansraj Dharamshala at PGI, Chandigarh.

‘’ TAMMANA’s Event 162 – ‘ PUNYA 2024’ , was dedicated to little children fighting Cancer & other long term ailments; bringing together their families who also go through a lot of struggle. PUNYA is the most looked forward to, distribution drive of the year. The team generously collected & distributed new blankets, toys , books & stationery kits for the NGO’s Annual event. In addition, Woolen caps, mufflers, gloves and also fruits were distributed to more than 200 people including children’’, shared Founder President Isha Kakaria.

The main hall of the dharamshala, which houses long-term patients who stay there on a daily charge to avoid travel for long term treatments was transformed into a festive space including a Christmas tree beautifully adorned by the children who enjoyed decorating it the most.

“Our aim was not only to create a home-away-from-home atmosphere but also to provide practical support through essential items like blankets and toys that bring comfort and joy,” said P Varuna, event SPOC and member of NGO Tammana. “The smiles we saw today made all our efforts worthwhile.”
The celebration featured a special appearance by member Yuvika Murali, as the Santa Claus of the day, who distributed the smiley balls to children singing jingles together.

The families expressed their gratitude for the initiative, noting how not just they are ready to brave the weather now , but also how such events and donations help boost morale and create a supportive environment for both patients & their families.

title: Blanket distribution
body: NGO Tammana, conducted yet another #blanket distribution drive for this winter ; for the labourers working in extreme weathers to meet their livelihood needs ; at 2 different, identified construction sites in Zirakpur. For Event # 163 of the NGO, a total of 200 blankets were distributed in association with Bebo Technologies.
From the team, Isha Kakaria , Jaskaran Singh, Naveen Pabreja , Saurabh Gulati, Kajal Sood and Nimrat Singh implemented the distribution smoothly’ shared office coordinator, Meenakshi Mahajan.

title: Lohri celebration at Aashray Home for the specially abled
body: Dressed in bright Phulkaris, Members at NGO Tammana, a dedicated non-profit organization, organized a vibrant Lohri celebration at Aashray Home for the specially abled, in Sector 47, Chandigarh. The event embraced the spirit of inclusivity by hosting 80 differently abled , including residents from Ashray Home & also from Samarth Jiyo. Isha Kakaria, the Founder President, expressed the profound purpose behind the event.

“Our primary objective is to raise awareness about disability inclusivity, fostering increased participation in socially expected life roles and activities. Autism spectrum disorder is a neurological and developmental disorder that affects how people interact with others, communicate, learn, and behave. Described as a “developmental disorder” because symptoms generally appear in the first two years of life.”

The event commenced following a warm meet and greet, whereby attendees gathered and danced around a vibrantly decorated bonfire, shared the event SPOC Karan Rana. The venue resonated with the beats of a lively Dhol, setting the platform for everyone to revel in the joyous occasion. The festivities continued with traditional folk songs sung by all, creating an atmosphere of unity and celebration. All were treated to tea and refreshments around the ceremonial bonfire.
Meenakshi Mahajan, Office Coordinator and a longstanding member, highlighted Tammana’s 16+ years of dedicated service to society.
“Tammana welcomes all without a fee, and those passionate about our cause can easily join by registering at www.tammana.org.in.”

title: Nature trail at Lake forest
body: Team Tammana traded in their lazy Sunday morning for a refreshing escape into nature! On February 16th, 2025, the team organized a ‘Nature Trail’ at the serene Lake Forest Reserve in Chandigarh as its Event #165. Alongside their families, NGO members embarked on a 10,000-step journey, rejuvenating their senses amidst stunning trees, lake views, and tranquil surroundings. The sweet sounds of birds filled the air with positive energy as the sun rose at its brightest, spreading warmth. The team was thrilled to spot peacocks, deers, hens, and more in their natural habitat. True to their eco-friendly spirit, the team ensured a plastic-free and litter-free outing. The memories captured will surely bring back happy memories for the team and inspire others to go outdoors & connect with nature!

title: NGO Tammana Celebrates World Laughter Day !
body: Tammana, a dedicated organization focused on promoting well-being and community engagement, celebrated World Laughter Day on Sunday, May 4, at Sukhna Lake, Chandigarh. The event aimed to harness the power of laughter to bring people together, reduce stress, and promote overall well-being by encouraging silly movements and playful games to lighten the mood.
The objective was to help passersby collect moments of laughter and have some stress-free time, providing a much-needed break from the complexities of daily life.

The celebration featured laughter yoga sessions, a “laughing out the longest” game, and a joke-sharing session. The team added an extra layer of fun by incorporating funny props like wigs, funny face painting, fake mustaches, clown noses, and goofy glasses, making everyone laugh out loud. Participants were recognized for their laughter and joy with titles such as “Best Belly Laugh,” “Giggle Champ,” “Silliest Smile,” and “Joy Spreader of the Day.” Priyanka Garg was particularly energetic, earning the title of Joy Spreader of the Day.
To spread smiles even further, smiley balls were distributed for free—adding a cheerful touch to the event while also serving as a simple tool to help release stress. shared Event SPOC Neha Joshi.

“Laughter is a universal language that can bridge gaps and bring people together. We’re thrilled to celebrate World Laughter Day and promote its benefits to our community,” said Isha Kakaria, Founder, Tammana NGO. She further added that since laughter has numerous benefits, including physical advantages like boosting immunity and reducing pain, mental benefits like reducing stress and anxiety, and social benefits like fostering connections and community bonding, this felt right to conduct.
Tammana was founded in 2008, and this event marks the 166th event of the NGO. Interested individuals can join the organization by filling out a form at www.tammana.org.in
For more information, please contact: 9646072207.

title: योग उत्सव’ (Yoga Utsav) by NGO Tammana Marks International Day of Yoga
body: योग उत्सव’ (Yoga Utsav) by NGO Tammana Marks International Day of Yoga

15 June, Chandigarh — Tammana, a renowned NGO with over 16 years of impactful community service, celebrated the International Day of Yoga with its 167th event, ‘योग उत्सव (Yoga Utsav)’, on 15th June at the serene Garden of Fragrance, Sector 36B, Chandigarh.

The early morning session, starting at 5 AM, welcomed participants of all ages and experience levels, uniting them in the spirit of wellness and harmony. Held amidst nature’s calm, the event featured expert-led yoga practices that energized both body and mind.

Isha Kakaria, Founder President of Tammana, shared: “Yoga Utsav was organised free to inspire more individuals to explore the many benefits of yoga—whether they’re beginners or seasoned practitioners seeking collective energy. Our 167th event marks another stride in our mission to promote holistic well-being. We are grateful to Dr. Manisha Sharma, Naturopath & a professional Social Worker, for conducting this beautiful session.”

Jasmine, the event coordinator, added: “The experience included not just yoga but also chanting and laughter sessions in a beautiful natural setting. Post the event, members played badminton to encourage outdoor physical activity. Participants brought their own mats, water bottles, and came dressed in comfortable attire.”

Fruits and fresh juices were served as healthy refreshments. The event aimed to promote physical fitness, mental clarity, and community spirit through the timeless practice of yoga, as highlighted by PR Executive P Varuna.

title: Sitaare Zameen Par
body: On Sunday, 29th June, NGO Tammana organised a heartwarming movie outing at PVR Zirakpur for children from humble backgrounds and under-served communities who are part of the NGO’s initiative, Project Yakeen.
The event aimed to provide 30 children with a joyful and meaningful break from their daily challenges — a day filled with inspiration, laughter, and hope, shared Event Coordinator Saurabh Gulati.

The children watched Sitare Zameen Par, a touching film that celebrates the dreams, struggles, and hidden talents of children who often feel left out or misunderstood. The story fostered empathy, inclusion, and reminded viewers of the importance of recognising each child’s unique potential. The screening left the young audience deeply moved and instilled in them a renewed sense of self-belief.

“The outing was not just about watching a film — it was a day filled with emotions, learning, and togetherness. Our team members ensured that every child felt included and cared for, making the day truly memorable,” — Isha Kakaria, Founder President, NGO Tammana
NGO Tammana remains committed to curating such enriching experiences that nurture the holistic growth and happiness of children — helping them dream bigger and brighter.

title: ”Raksha For Nature” – A Rakhi Tied to Our Planet
body: This Raksha Bandhan, NGO Tammana launched a thoughtful and inspiring initiative titled “Raksha For Nature”, a symbolic act of tying a rakhi not just to our loved ones, but also to Mother Earth.

In today’s world where our connection with nature is rapidly fading, this campaign stood as a reminder that just as we vow to protect our loved ones, we must also take responsibility for protecting the Earth.
It was more than a campaign. It was a noble movement rooted in awareness, gratitude, and action.
The initiative aimed to:
• Spread awareness about environmental responsibility
• Encourage individuals of all ages to reconnect with nature
• Transform a traditional festival into a meaningful environmental action
• Bring families together through a shared activity of planting saplings

The event saw enthusiastic participation from Tammana’s core team members, numerous interns, public volunteers, and their family members, including young children. Each participant planted one or more saplings at their home or in a nearby park ; a small act with a big impact.
Every sapling planted symbolized a promise for a safer, greener, and more conscious tomorrow.
Every single contribution mattered, and that’s the true success of this movement.
Founder President Isha Kakaria shared :
“Raksha For Nature is more than a celebration. It’s a seed of responsibility sown in every heart, towards love, awareness, and gratitude for nature.”

title: ASHIA 17 – The Annual Awards Night by NGO Tammana
body: ASHIA 17 – The Annual Awards Night by NGO Tammana
Light beyond the Dark

With hearts full of gratitude and spirits soaring high, NGO Tammana celebrated its 17th anniversary with ASHIA 17 – an evening dedicated to honouring selfless service, compassion, and the journey of giving.
In true Tammana tradition, the event began with the candle-lighting ceremony, also symbolising the event’s theme “Light Beyond the Dark.”
The aura of the evening was elevated with a cake-cutting celebration, while everyone dressed spooky in black, danced their hearts out along with their family members, adding joy & laughter.
The night sparkled with the Annual 7 Star Awards and Superstar Awards, recognising members for their dedication and impact. Adding to the excitement, new award categories were introduced this year.

The Red Warriors Award for outstanding blood donation contribution was proudly presented to Naveen Pabreja, Jaskaran Singh, and Nimrat Singh Saini. The SPOC of the Year Award was conferred upon Vagabond Singh for his exemplary leadership and commitment, while Neha Joshi was honoured as Tammanaite of the Year 2025, celebrating her inspiring efforts & dedication.
The evening also witnessed the distribution of Experience Certifications, marking milestones of service.
The awards were presented by Founder President, Isha Kakaria and General Secretary, Jaskaran Singh, adding a personal touch to the honours.
Speaking on the occasion, Founder President Isha Kakaria said,

“Tammana was founded in 2008 with a vision to create meaningful change, and over these 17 years we have touched countless lives with compassion and service. Each milestone reflects the strength of our volunteers and the belief that together, we can always do more.”

The celebrations concluded with a heartfelt Shukrana at Sai Mandir, Sector 29, Chandigarh, to offer prayers, gratitude, blessings, and strength for the journey ahead as NGO Tammana entered its 18th year!

title: Visit to Prabh Aasra with Jubilee
body: NGO Tammana, in collaboration with Jubilee Real Estate Group, visited Prabh Aasra, Jhanjeri yesterday; a shelter home for the elderly, specially-abled, and for all those in need.

The day was filled with warmth as Members @naveenpabreja (along with his son) and Parul Malik stepped forward, interacted, played, danced, and shared countless moments of joy with the residents. Their efforts and time are deeply appreciated.
Basic necessities and thoughtful gifts were distributed by the corporate, further adding comfort and smiles.
Our heartfelt appreciation to Member @jaskaran_singh_06 for making this collaboration possible.

title: NGO Tammana Celebrates Diwali with ‘Light A Life’
body: NGO Tammana successfully organized its 172nd event, “Light A Life,” on Sunday, 12th October 2025, at Village Singhpura, Zirakpur, bringing together volunteers and children to celebrate the spirit of Diwali with creativity and compassion.

The event featured a diya painting session, where children joyfully painted and decorated diyas alongside Tammana volunteers. The beautifully crafted diyas were later distributed, spreading light and happiness across the community. The celebration also included the distribution of gifts, refreshments, and sweets, making the day memorable for everyone present.

Through this initiative, NGO Tammana once again demonstrated its commitment to fostering inclusivity, creativity, and togetherness. The event not only brightened homes with diyas but also hearts with smiles and festive cheer.

“Light A Life” reflected the true essence of Diwali — sharing joy, hope, and love with those around us. NGO Tammana’s continued efforts to uplift communities and create meaningful social connections made this celebration a shining example of how small acts of kindness can make a big difference.
